claims.claim: Cleveland-Cliffs links domestic iron ore, pellets/DRI, primary steelmaking and downstream finishing to automotive, infrastructure and manufacturing demand; vertical integration reduces some upstream dependency but does not remove steel-cycle or end-market demand sensitivity.

The structural resilience case depends on domestic capacity scarcity and customer need for specialized sheet/electrical/stainless/plate products; substitutes include imported steel, alternative domestic mills and material-lighting/substitution in end products.

causalEdges: iron ore/DRI integration -> input security -> steel production

risks.risk: Vertical integration cannot insulate cash flow from automotive and steel-price cycles.

unknowns.unknown: Durability of current domestic pricing/volume support under future trade-policy regimes remains uncertain.

claims.claim: Q2 2026 improved materially from Q1, with adjusted EBITDA of $286M and positive free cash flow, but automotive still represented 29% of steelmaking revenue and the company explicitly retains steel-cycle, trade-policy, indebtedness and project-execution risks.

A domestic-scarcity thesis would be weakened if imports rise materially, automotive demand falls, or debt reduction stalls despite improved EBITDA; current Q2 evidence does not establish those falsifiers as realized.

causalEdges: auto demand decline -> lower steel volumes
positive FCF -> debt reduction -> improved resilience

risks.risk: Automotive concentration remains material at 29% of Q2 steelmaking revenue.
Debt and capital-project execution can limit flexibility through a cyclical downturn.

unknowns.unknown: Whether Q3 guidance converts into sustained free cash flow and meaningful debt reduction remains future execution.
